name: Nvidia

summary.text: Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) designs graphics processors and AI accelerated-computing platforms for data centers, gaming, professional visualization and automotive. Jen-Hsun (Jensen) Huang founded it in 1993 and is its President, CEO and a director. Its FY2026 revenue was $215.9 billion. Its sales of advanced chips to China depend on U.S. government licenses and Commerce Department rules.

facts.claim: Nvidia's 10-K states that it is defending a securities class action brought by shareholders who allege false or misleading statements about channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand in 2017 and 2018.
facts.quote: we are defending a securities class action lawsuit from multiple shareholders asserting claims that we and certain of our officers made false and/or misleading statements related to channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand in 2017 and 2018.

sources.title: NVIDIA Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, filed 2026-02-25

facts.claim: Nvidia's 10-K states that in August 2025 the U.S. government granted licenses allowing shipments of certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, generating approximately $60 million in H20 revenue, and that U.S. officials expected the government to receive 15% or more of licensed sales revenue, which was not published as a regulation.
facts.quote: In August 2025, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers. We generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses. USG officials expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% or more of the revenue generated from licensed sales of our products, but the USG did not publish a regulation codifying such requirement.

sources.title: NVIDIA Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, filed 2026-02-25

facts.claim: Nvidia's 10-K states that in February 2026 the U.S. government granted a license allowing small H200 shipments to specific China-based customers, and that Nvidia had not yet generated revenue under the H200 licensing program.
facts.quote: In February 2026, the USG granted a license that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers. To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program

sources.title: NVIDIA Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, filed 2026-02-25

facts.claim: Nvidia's 10-K states that under current rules it is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China's data center market that receives approval from both the U.S. and Chinese governments.
facts.quote: Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China s data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government.

sources.title: NVIDIA Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, filed 2026-02-25

facts.claim: Nvidia reported full-year fiscal 2026 revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65%, and stated that it is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.
facts.quote: Record full-year revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65%. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.

facts.quote: changing it from a presumption of denial to a case-by-case review. The semiconductors covered by this rule are the Nvidia H200 and its equivalents

openQuestions: Share classes: the 2026 proxy and 10-K report a single class of common stock (24,220,525,225 shares outstanding). No dual-class structure is recorded because no source opened states one.
Institutional holders beyond the 5% holders: only BlackRock and Vanguard appear in the proxy table; other holders were not verified.
Individual director backgrounds and committee roles were not separately verified beyond the nominee list.

15% China revenue-share: the 10-K attributes this to U.S. officials' expectation, not a codified regulation. The reported August 2025 Nvidia-AMD arrangement via Reuters was NOT verified (Reuters returns 401 to fetch and browser).
Export-license revenue exposure in dollar terms beyond the approximately $60 million H20 figure, and government contract awards: USAspending GET rejected; sam.gov unreachable.
BIS enforcement actions or penalties against Nvidia: none found in the Federal Register API search; not recorded.
Outside lobbying firms (The Nickles Group, Tiber Creek Group, Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck, BGR Government Affairs) appear in LDA filings; totals were not summed and are not recorded.
China antitrust: the 10-K describes a preliminary regulator finding; not verified in a primary Chinese regulator source and NOT recorded as a fact.
U.S. and EU antitrust: no DOJ, FTC or European Commission proceeding against Nvidia was confirmed (justice.gov 404, ftc.gov 403, EC press page renders empty).
Groq: the 10-K describes a non-exclusive license; no second source confirmed the characterization.
Co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem are not named in any source opened; not recorded.
